The Brothers McKAY,FRED STONE, JIMMY FLATT and MICK PYER came into the fold in 1921,and 1922 gave us WALLY BAYLISS (Hon. Secretary for eleven years and President for three), the incomparable BERT FOOTER, and champion walker HAROLD KING.

The start of the 1926 Surrey County Championship at Epsom Downs which Belgrave (79pts) won from Epsom (81 pts) and Surrey AC (93pts). Our six scorers were Ken O'Kell (3rd), Micky Pyer (4th), Bert Footer (8th), J.

In 1922, Jimmy was second in the Club 7-miles cross-country championship, but went one better the following year, when he won the "Blackstaffe" Shield. Second to him on that occasion was Micky Pyer, and third Bert Footer. In 1924, he took third medal in this championship.

In only his second match for Belgrave he closed-in our scoring team just behind first-team regulars Wally Bayliss and Micky Pyer. Ken O'Kell, together with Bill Webb, Bert Footer and Micky Pyer, was a key figure in Belgrave's cross-country revival in the early "twenties"; winning an individual bronze medal in the Surrey County C.C.

On the 21st October 1991 MICKY PYER became the first ever Belgravian to reach 70 years of unbroken membership. He has seen many eras come and go, and played no small part in our teams of the twenties which did so much to prepare the way for their victorious successors of the thirties.
.... and Harry Porter received the following letter from Micky Pyer's daughter.
Micky Pyer had set the standard by winning the Surrey County mile title and finishing runner-up in the South of Thames Junior cross-country race in 1922.
I am sorry to hear that Micky Pyer is not well. I send him my warmest regards and best wishes for his recovery.

It was nice to see Micky Pyer up at the Hall with his daughter one Saturday in September. Bob Glover was seen the other day in the vicinity of Lauriston Road, he looked pretty well but wouldn't call in at the Hall for a 'cuppa'.

Charlie recalls that the first meeting he ever saw was in 1921, also at Battersea, when Micky Pyer won a mile championship race. In those days there was a putting green where the car park now is, and for big meetings the Club used to get permission to erect a marquee on it for changing facilities.
